reasoning: In March 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol—an 18-time world champion and one of the most dominant Go players in history—by a score of 4 games to 1. Prior to AlphaGo's sudden success (which began with its secret defeat of European champion Fan Hui in late 2015, published in early 2016), artificial intelligence experts and Go professionals widely predicted that a computer program beating a top human professional at Go was at least a decade away. This is because Go has an enormous search space and requires intuitive evaluation, making traditional brute-force search methods ineffective.
